1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973("Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 505/2014 registered at Police Station Badarpur, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC").
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Amit Ahlawat, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Nachiketa Choudhary and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Jitendra Kumar from Police Station Badarpur, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that due to some matrimonial disputes between the parties,
respondent no.2 made complaint against the petitioners, upon which an FIR bearing No. 505/2014 for offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 IPC at Police Station Badadur was registered.

sentences.text: the parties had amicably settled their disputes and entered into a Settlement Deed dated 12.04.2022.

Pursuant to the settlement, parties obtained divorce by mutual consent vide Judgment and Decree dated 06.08.2022.
7.

On the query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties and she has no objection if FIR is quashed.

8. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 35,00,000/- in four installments in the following manner:
a.
First installment of Rs.5 Lakhs paid to respondent no.2 at the time of signing of MOU.
b. Second installment of Rs. 5 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of First Motion.

c. Third installment of Rs. 5 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of Second Motion.
e. Fourth/Final instalment of Rs. 20 lakhs to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.
10.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 20 Lacs today, i.e.,19.01.2023 by way of demand drafts in the following manner:-

, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 505/2014 registered at Police Station Badarpur, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The petition stands disposed of.
14. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
